2607.04223.title: Detecting Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Grounding-Aware Sensitivity by Perturbation (GASP)
2607.04223.paper_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduces but does not eliminate hallucination, and existing detectors return a single answer-level score that does not indicate which sentence is unsupported, or why. To close this gap, we introduce Grounding-Aware Sensitivity by Perturbation (GASP), a span-level detector that scores each answer sentence by how strongly its likelihood depends on the retrieved evidence, a quantity we term grounding sensitivity. GASP holds the answer fixed and re-scores it under the full context, under no context, and with each chunk removed, then measures the log-likelihood drops and Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD). The likelihood of a grounded sentence collapses once its supporting passage is removed, whereas a hallucinated sentence is almost unaffected, a contrast we interpret by casting decoding as a random nonlinear iterated function system (RNIFS). We evaluate GASP on three benchmarks (RAGTruth, TofuEval, RAGBench) with three instruction-tuned scorers from two model families (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and SmolLM2-1.7B) under a leakage-clean protocol. On RAGTruth it reaches a response-level area under the ROC curve (AUC) of about 0.73 and a span-level AUC of about 0.67, improving significantly over perplexity and by clear margins over length, whole-context natural language inference (NLI), and self-consistency baselines. The only baseline competitive at the span level is a well-configured chunk-level entailment verifier, which requires a separate model, whereas a training-free threshold on the grounding features matches the trained classifier without labeled data and serves as the default detector. Beyond RAGTruth, the signal transfers to TofuEval but not to short-answer question answering in RAGBench, showing GASP is best suited to outputs constructed from the retrieved context rather than answers recoverable from parametric knowledge.
2607.04223.paper_summary_zh: 檢索增強生成（RAG）減少但並不消除幻覺，現有的檢測器返回一個單一的答案級別分數，無法指示哪個句子是沒有支持的，或為什麼。為了填補這一空白，我們引入了基於擾動的基礎感知（GASP），這是一個範圍級檢測器，根據每個答案句子對檢索證據的依賴程度來評分，我們稱之為基礎敏感性。GASP 固定答案，並在完整上下文、無上下文以及每個片段被移除的情況下重新評分，然後測量對數似然下降和詹森-香農散度（JSD）。一旦支持段落被移除，基礎句子的似然性就會崩潰，而幻覺句子幾乎不受影響，我們通過將解碼視為隨機非線性迭代函數系統（RNIFS）來解釋這一對比。我們在三個基準（RAGTruth、TofuEval、RAGBench）上評估 GASP，使用來自兩個模型系列的三個指令調整評分器（Qwen2.5-0.5B、Qwen2.5-1.5B 和 SmolLM2-1.7B），遵循泄漏清理協議。在 RAGTruth 上，它達到了約 0.73 的響應級 ROC 曲線下面積（AUC）和約 0.67 的範圍級 AUC，顯著改善了困惑度，並在長度、整體上下文自然語言推理（NLI）和自一致性基準上有明顯的優勢。唯一在範圍級具有競爭力的基準是一個配置良好的片段級包含驗證器，這需要一個單獨的模型，而在基礎特徵上的無訓練閾值則能匹配訓練的分類器，無需標記數據，並作為默認檢測器。超越 RAGTruth，信號轉移到 TofuEval，但未轉移到 RAGBench 的短答案問題回答，顯示 GASP 最適合從檢索上下文構建的輸出，而不是從參數知識中恢復的答案。
